literal: In the first year of Zhenjun she bore Gaozong.
idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenjun she bore Gaozong.

literal: In Shizu's last years she died.
idiomatic: She died in Shizu's last years.

literal: When Gaozong took the throne he raised her posthumous title.
idiomatic: When Gaozong took the throne he raised her posthumous title.

literal: Burial at Jinling in Yunzhong; paired sacrifice in the Grand Temple.
idiomatic: She was buried at Jinling in Yunzhong and paired in the Grand Temple.

literal: Gaozong's wet-nurse Lady Chang was originally from Liaoxi.
idiomatic: Gaozong's wet-nurse, Lady Chang, came from Liaoxi.

literal: In Taiyan she entered the palace on business; Shizu chose her to nurse Gaozong.
idiomatic: In Taiyan she entered the palace; Shizu chose her to nurse Gaozong.

literal: Kind and compliant in conduct, she had merit in toilsome care and protection.
idiomatic: Gentle and dutiful, she earned merit through exhausting care.

literal: When Gaozong took the throne she was honored as Foster Empress Dowager, soon Empress Dowager, with rites at the suburban altars.
idiomatic: When Gaozong took the throne she was honored foster empress dowager, then empress dowager, with rites at the suburban altars.

literal: In the first year of Heping she died; an edict ordered three days of great mourning throughout the realm; posthumous title Zhao; burial at Mojie Mountain in Guangning—popularly called Cock-crow Mountain—by the empress dowager's own wish.
idiomatic: She died in the first year of Heping; the realm mourned three days; posthumous title Zhao; she was buried at Mojie Mountain in Guangning, popularly Cock-crow Mountain, as she had wished.

literal: Following Foster Empress Dowager Hui's precedent, a separate sleeping temple was built; two hundred households were set to guard the tomb; a stele praised her virtue.
idiomatic: Following Foster Empress Dowager Hui's precedent, a separate temple was built, two hundred households guarded the tomb, and a stele praised her virtue.

literal: Empress Wenhua of Emperor Wencheng, Lady Feng, was a native of Xindu in Changle.
idiomatic: Emperor Wencheng's Empress Wenhua, née Feng, came from Xindu in Changle.

literal: Her father Lang was governor of Qin and Yong provinces and Duke of Xicheng; [8] her mother was Lady Wang of Lelang.
idiomatic: Her father Lang was governor of Qin and Yong and duke of Xicheng; [8] her mother was Lady Wang of Lelang.

literal: The empress was born at Chang'an; there was a wonder of divine light.
idiomatic: She was born at Chang'an amid a wonder of divine light.

literal: Lang was executed for an offense; the empress then entered the palace.
idiomatic: When Lang was executed for a crime she entered the palace.

literal: Shizu's Left Worthy Lady was the empress's aunt; she had true motherly virtue in rearing and teaching.
idiomatic: Shizu's left worthy lady was her aunt and raised her with motherly care.

literal: At fourteen, when Gaozong took the throne, she was chosen Honored Person; later she was made empress.
idiomatic: At fourteen, when Gaozong took the throne, she became honored person; later empress.

literal: When Gaozong died, by precedent: on great mourning, after three days all imperial garments and vessels were burned; officials and the inner palace all wailed and attended.
idiomatic: When Gaozong died, precedent held that after three days all imperial garments and vessels were burned while officials and the inner palace wailed over them.

literal: The empress in grief threw herself into the fire; attendants saved her; long before she revived.
idiomatic: Grieving, she threw herself into the fire; attendants pulled her out; long passed before she revived.

literal: When Xianzu took the throne she was honored as Empress Dowager.
idiomatic: When Xianzu took the throne she was honored empress dowager.

literal: Chief Minister Yi Hun plotted rebellion; Xianzu was twelve, [9] in the mourning hut; the empress dowager secretly settled the great plan, executed Hun, and then held court and heard affairs.
idiomatic: Chief Minister Yi Hun plotted treason; Xianzu was twelve, [9] in mourning seclusion; the empress dowager secretly settled the plot, killed Hun, and took the regency.

literal: When Gaozu was born the empress dowager personally reared him.
idiomatic: When Gaozu was born she reared him herself.

literal: Afterward she ceased edicts and did not hear affairs.
idiomatic: Afterward she stopped issuing edicts and withdrew from government.

literal: The empress dowager's conduct was improper; she favored Li Yi within; Xianzu executed him on a pretext; the empress dowager was displeased.
idiomatic: She kept an improper favorite, Li Yi; Xianzu killed him on a pretext; she was displeased.

literal: Xianzu died suddenly; at the time people said the empress dowager had done it.
idiomatic: Xianzu died suddenly; rumor said the empress dowager was responsible.

literal: In the first year of Chengming she was honored Grand Empress Dowager and again held court and heard affairs.
idiomatic: In the first year of Chengming she became grand empress dowager and ruled again.

literal: The empress dowager was intelligent and penetrating; from entering the rear palace she had roughly learned writing and reckoning.
idiomatic: Clever and penetrating, she had learned basic writing and reckoning in the palace.

literal: When she reached supreme rank she decided the myriad affairs.
idiomatic: At supreme rank she decided every affair of state.

literal: Gaozu's edict said: "We, empty and few, in youth inherited the precious succession, relying on motherly clarity to settle the four seas; to repay such virtue only the true awakening suffices; all birds of prey and creatures that harm life should be released to mountains and forests.
idiomatic: Gaozu decreed: "We inherited the throne young, relying on her clarity to settle the realm; to repay her virtue we release birds of prey and all creatures that harm life to the mountains.

literal: Let this place be the site where the Grand Empress Dowager first raised her spirit pagoda.
idiomatic: Let this ground be where the grand empress dowager first raised her spirit pagoda."

literal: Thereupon the Hawk Office was abolished and the land became Repaying Virtue Buddhist Temple.
idiomatic: The hawk office was abolished and the land became Repaying Virtue Buddhist Temple.

literal: The empress dowager toured Mount Fang with Gaozu; gazing at rivers and hills she had the will to end her days there, and said to the ministers: "When Shun was buried at Cangwu, the two consorts did not follow.
idiomatic: Touring Mount Fang with Gaozu she looked on river and hill and chose it for her rest, telling the ministers: "When Shun was buried at Cangwu his two consorts did not follow.

literal: Must one be buried far at the imperial tombs to be honored?
idiomatic: Must one lie far at the imperial tombs to be honored?"

literal: After my hundred years let my spirit rest here.
idiomatic: When my hundred years are done let my spirit rest here."

literal: Gaozu then ordered the offices to build her longevity tomb at Mount Fang and raise the Eternal Firm stone hall, intending it ultimately as a pure temple.
idiomatic: Gaozu ordered her longevity tomb built at Mount Fang and the Eternal Firm stone hall raised, meant in the end as a pure temple.

literal: Construction began in the fifth year of Taihe and was finished in the eighth; stone was carved and a stele set up praising the empress dowager's merit.
idiomatic: Work began in the fifth year of Taihe and finished in the eighth; stone was carved and a stele praised her merit.

literal: Because Gaozu was in the prime of youth the empress dowager composed more than three hundred chapters of admonitory songs and eighteen chapters of imperial instructions; most of the text is not recorded.
idiomatic: While Gaozu was young she wrote more than three hundred admonitory songs and eighteen imperial instructions; most are not preserved.

literal: The empress dowager built the temple of Prince Wenhua at Chang'an, [10] and also the Siyan Buddha hall at Longcheng; both had stone carved and steles set up.
idiomatic: She built Prince Wenhua's temple at Chang'an [10] and the Siyan Buddha hall at Longcheng, each with carved stone and stele.

literal: The empress dowager also decreed: inner five-temple grandsons and outer kin within six degrees of mourning all received mourning leave.
idiomatic: She also decreed mourning leave for inner five-temple grandsons and outer kin within six degrees.

literal: By nature frugal and plain, she disliked ornament and wore only plain silk herself.
idiomatic: Frugal by nature, she disliked ornament and wore only plain silk.

literal: When stewards served food the tray was barely a foot across; delicacies were reduced to eight-tenths of precedent.
idiomatic: Trays for her meals were barely a foot wide; delicacies were cut to eight-tenths of precedent.

literal: The empress dowager once, feeling unwell, took crow-dipper seeds.
idiomatic: Once, feeling unwell, she took crow-dipper seeds.

literal: A steward at dusk brought porridge; a gecko was in it; the empress raised her spoon and found it.
idiomatic: At dusk a steward brought porridge with a gecko in it; she found it with her spoon.

literal: Gaozu attended at her side, greatly angered, and meant extreme punishment; the empress dowager smiled and released him.
idiomatic: Gaozu beside her was furious and meant extreme punishment; she smiled and let the man go.

literal: From the empress dowager's sole regency Gaozu by nature was filial and cautious and did not wish to decide; whether great or small, all followed the empress dowager.
idiomatic: Under her sole rule Gaozu was filial and cautious and would not decide; great and small, all went to her.

literal: The empress dowager was resourceful, suspicious, and cruel, able to act on great matters; life, death, reward, and punishment were decided in a moment, often without Gaozu's knowledge.
idiomatic: She was resourceful, suspicious, and cruel, deciding life, death, reward, and punishment in a moment, often without telling Gaozu.

literal: Thus authority and favor together shook inner and outer.
idiomatic: Authority and favor together shook court and realm.

literal: Thus Wang Yu, Zhang You, Fu Chengzu, and others were raised from humble eunuchs to princes and dukes within the year;
idiomatic: Wang Yu, Zhang You, Fu Chengzu, and others rose from humble eunuchs to princes and dukes within a year;

literal: Wang Rui went in and out of the sleeping quarters; within years he was chief minister; rewards of wealth in the hundreds of millions; golden writ on iron covenant promising an edict of deathlessness.
idiomatic: Wang Rui entered the sleeping quarters and within years became chief minister, rewarded with wealth in the hundreds of millions and a golden writ on iron promising he could not be executed.

literal: Though Li Chong was employed for ability, it was also through favor within the curtains and secret bestowals beyond counting.
idiomatic: Li Chong won office for talent, but also through secret favor and gifts beyond counting.

literal: The empress dowager's nature was strict and clear; even when she showed favor she did not indulge.
idiomatic: She was strict and clear; even favorites were not indulged.

literal: For the slightest fault of attendants she often added beating—more than a hundred strokes, fewer several tens.
idiomatic: The slightest fault in attendants could bring a hundred strokes or several tens.

literal: Yet she did not harbor old resentment; soon she treated them as before, or they grew richer for it.
idiomatic: Yet she did not hold grudges; soon she treated them as before, or they grew richer.

literal: Thus everyone clung to profit and desire and to the end did not think of withdrawal.
idiomatic: Everyone clung to profit and never thought of leaving.

literal: The empress dowager once with Gaozu visited Spirit Spring Pool, feasted ministers and envoys of border states and chieftains of all regions, each ordered to perform his region's dance.
idiomatic: She once feasted ministers and foreign envoys at Spirit Spring Pool and had each perform his region's dance.

literal: Gaozu led the ministers in offering longevity; the empress dowager gladly made a song; the emperor harmonized; then she ordered each to state his aim—and ninety harmonized.
idiomatic: Gaozu led longevity toasts; she sang gladly; he harmonized; then each stated his aim—and ninety sang in reply.

literal: The empress dowager outwardly honored men the people looked to—Yuan Pi, You Minggen, and others—and bestowed gold, silk, carriages, and horses; whenever she praised Rui and the like she had Pi and others present to show lack of partiality.
idiomatic: Outwardly she honored Yuan Pi, You Minggen, and others the people respected, bestowing gold and horses; when she praised Rui she had Pi present to show impartiality.

literal: Again, fearing criticism of her faults, at the slightest suspicion she saw execution.
idiomatic: Fearing criticism, she killed at the slightest suspicion.

literal: Until the empress dowager's death Gaozu did not know how he was born.
idiomatic: Until her death Gaozu did not know the truth of his birth.

literal: As for Li Xin, Li Hui, and the like—more than ten houses destroyed through suspicion—several hundred dead, mostly wrongful; the realm mourned them.
idiomatic: Li Xin, Li Hui, and more than ten houses fell to suspicion; hundreds died, mostly innocent; the realm mourned them.

literal: In the fourteenth year she died in the Taihe Hall at age forty-nine.
idiomatic: In the fourteenth year she died in the Taihe Hall at forty-nine.

literal: That day a male pheasant alighted on the Taihua Hall.
idiomatic: That day a male pheasant alighted on the Taihua Hall.

literal: Gaozu drank but did not eat for five days; mourning exceeded ritual.
idiomatic: Gaozu drank but did not eat for five days; his mourning exceeded ritual.

literal: Posthumous title: Grand Empress Dowager Wenhua.
idiomatic: Her posthumous title was Grand Empress Dowager Wenhua.

literal: Burial at the Eternal Firm tomb; at midday the procession returned; offering at the Jianxuan Hall.
idiomatic: She was buried at the Eternal Firm tomb; at noon the procession returned; rites were at the Jianxuan Hall.

literal: An edict said: "The honored will followed frugality; boundless grief was not expressed;
idiomatic: An edict said: "Her honored will was frugal; boundless grief could not be fully shown;

literal: fitting feeling and allowable ritual upward diminish the teaching of frugality.
idiomatic: yet fitting feeling and allowable ritual still tempered frugal teaching."

literal: Advancing and retreating in thought, grief redoubled at the collapse.
idiomatic: Thinking it through, grief redoubled at her death.

literal: Again, for mountain-tomb rites there were settled orders: within a square zhang, without only covering the pit—yet where the filial son's heart could not be fully satisfied, the inner chamber might be two zhang and the mound not more than thirty-odd paces.
idiomatic: For the tomb she had ordered a square zhang within and only a covering mound without—yet where a son's heart fell short the inner chamber might be two zhang and the mound thirty-odd paces.

literal: Now the mountain tomb is looked to for ten thousand generations and is again broadened to sixty paces.
idiomatic: Now the tomb is looked to for ten thousand generations and is broadened to sixty paces.

literal: Failing the last will, grief is all the more cutting.
idiomatic: Failing her last will, grief cuts deeper.

literal: The inner chamber's size, coffin quality plain and simple, no bright vessels set out.
idiomatic: The inner chamber, coffin, and goods stay plain; no bright grave goods.

literal: Even plain curtains, plain mats, porcelain tiles—none are placed.
idiomatic: Even plain curtains, mats, and porcelain—none are placed.

literal: This follows the former will and the written order; both honor the legacy.
idiomatic: This follows her will and the written order; both honor her legacy.

literal: Yet where there is compliance and where departure, those who do not understand may find it strange.
idiomatic: Where we comply and where we depart, some may find it strange.

literal: Within the imperial coffin, in the dark hall, the sage spirit relies—therefore each point is followed to display frugal virtue.
idiomatic: Within the coffin and dark hall her spirit rests—there we follow each point to show frugal virtue.

literal: For other outer matters where there is non-compliance, it is to exhaust the feeling of painful longing.
idiomatic: Outer matters we bend to exhaust painful longing.

literal: Let this be proclaimed far and near and set forth to all offices: above to clarify the good of frugal teaching, below to show the fault of disobeying the command."
idiomatic: Let this be proclaimed far and near: above to clarify frugal teaching, below to show where we disobeyed."

literal: At the end of wailing Gaozu wore mourning; close attendants followed; third-rank ministers and below in outer mourning changed to finer hemp; seventh-rank and below removed mourning and returned to normal dress.
idiomatic: After wailing Gaozu wore mourning; close attendants followed; outer officials third rank and below changed to finer hemp; seventh rank and below returned to normal dress.

literal: Associated sacrifice was set in the Taihe Hall; from dukes and ministers down they first attended to public affairs.
idiomatic: Associated sacrifice was set in the Taihe Hall; from dukes down they resumed public business.

literal: Gaozu wasted away, abstained from wine and meat, and did not take inner attendants for three years.
idiomatic: Gaozu wasted away, took no wine or meat, and kept no inner attendants for three years.

literal: At first Gaozu was filial toward the empress dowager; therefore a little more than a li northeast of the Eternal Firm tomb he beforehand built a longevity palace, with the will to gaze there at the end.
idiomatic: Filial toward her, he had built a longevity palace a little over a li northeast of her tomb, intending to rest his gaze there at the end.

literal: When he moved the capital to Luoyang he himself memorialized the west bank of the Chan as the mountain garden site; the empty hall at Mount Fang remains to this day, called the Hall of Ten Thousand Years.
idiomatic: When he moved to Luoyang he chose the west bank of the Chan for his own mountain garden; the empty hall at Mount Fang remains, called the Hall of Ten Thousand Years.

literal: Primary Empress of Emperor Wencheng, Lady Li, was a native of Meng in Liang; sister to Prince Jun of Dunqiu.
idiomatic: Emperor Wencheng's primary empress, née Li, came from Meng in Liang; she was sister to Prince Jun of Dunqiu.

literal: [11] At her birth there was wonder beyond the usual; her father Fangshu always said this girl would be greatly honored.
idiomatic: [11] Her birth was wondrous; her father Fangshu always said she would rise to great honor.

literal: When grown, her bearing and beauty were fine.
idiomatic: Grown, she was beautiful in bearing.

literal: When Shizu campaigned south, Prince Yongchang Ren marched from Shouchun; the army reached her home and took her.
idiomatic: When Shizu marched south, Prince Yongchang Ren left Shouchun; his army reached her home and took her.

literal: When Ren was stationed at Chang'an he was executed for an affair; she and her family were sent to the palace at Pingcheng.
idiomatic: When Ren was stationed at Chang'an he was executed; she and her family were sent to the Pingcheng palace.

literal: Gaozong ascended the White Tower, saw her, admired her, and said to attendants: "Is this woman not fine?
idiomatic: Gaozong on the White Tower saw her, admired her, and asked attendants: "Is she not fine?"

literal: All said "Indeed."
idiomatic: All said, "Indeed."

literal: He descended; she won favor in the fasting storehouse and became pregnant.
idiomatic: He descended; she won favor in the fasting storehouse and became pregnant.

literal: Foster Empress Dowager Chang later questioned her; she said: "The emperor favored me and I am still pregnant."
idiomatic: Foster Empress Dowager Chang later questioned her; she said the emperor had favored her and she was pregnant.

literal: The storekeeper had also privately written on the wall; separate questioning matched in every point.
idiomatic: The storekeeper had privately written on the wall; separate questioning matched.

literal: When she bore Xianzu she was made Honored Person.
idiomatic: When she bore Xianzu she was made honored person.

literal: In the second year of Tai'an the empress dowager ordered by precedent that the empress fully record her brothers in the south and sworn clan brother Hongzhi, all to be entrusted.
idiomatic: In the second year of Tai'an the empress dowager ordered her, by precedent, to record her southern brothers and sworn clan brother Hongzhi for entrustment.

literal: At the farewell, each time she named a brother she beat her breast and wept bitterly; then she died.
idiomatic: At the farewell each brother's name brought breast-beating tears; then she died.

literal: Later posthumous title Primary Empress; burial at Jinling; paired sacrifice in the Grand Temple.
idiomatic: Later she received the posthumous title Primary Empress, burial at Jinling, and pairing in the Grand Temple.

literal: Empress Si of Emperor Xianwen, Lady Li, was a native of Anxi in Zhongshan; daughter of Prince Hui of Nanyang.
idiomatic: Emperor Xianwen's Empress Si, née Li, came from Anxi in Zhongshan; daughter of Prince Hui of Nanyang.

literal: Graceful in bearing and virtue, at eighteen she was chosen into the Eastern Palace.
idiomatic: Graceful in bearing and virtue, at eighteen she entered the eastern palace.

literal: When Xianzu took the throne she was Lady and bore Gaozu.
idiomatic: When Xianzu took the throne she was a lady and bore Gaozu.

literal: In the third year of Huangxing she died; above and below none did not mourn.
idiomatic: In the third year of Huangxing she died; court and realm mourned.
